sections.title: The 'Why': Explicit vs. Implicit Curves
lecture_lines: Explicit functions like y=f(x) are easy.
Implicit curves hide variables like y=y(x).
Sometimes solving for y is impossible.
animations: Create a 2D plot showing an explicit curve y=f(x) in #FFFFFF color.
Change the explicit curve to an implicit curve f(x,y)=0.
Highlight the difference between the two forms with #FF0000.

sections.title: The Core Concept: The Chain Rule
lecture_lines: Recall the chain rule for derivatives.
Treat y as an inner function, y(x).
animations: Display the equation dy/dx = dy/du * du/dx in #FFFFFF.
Animate each term of the chain rule in distinct colors.
Show a small increment dx resulting in dy.

sections.title: The 3-Step Procedure
lecture_lines: Differentiate both sides with respect to x.
animations: Show the first step: Differentiate both sides of equation.
Show the second step: Group all dy/dx terms together.
Show the third step: Solve for dy/dx explicitly.

sections.title: Visual Application: Tangent Lines
lecture_lines: Consider the Folium of Descartes curve.
Use dy/dx to find tangent line.
animations: Draw an implicit curve and a point on it.
Calculate and draw the tangent line at that point.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
lecture_lines: Always tag y terms with dy/dx.
Verify your answer with the derivative.
animations: Summarize the three steps in a text box.
Flash the final formula for dy/dx.
Display a checkmark icon to conclude.
